findings.piece: Calculator labels: what the converted gradient is (old page and front-page quick calculator)
findings.says: The old page labels its second field "Pressure Gradient (mmHg)", and the intro says it converts "between peak velocity and pressure gradient". The quick calculator's field is "Pressure gradient" and its headline reads "x.xx m/s ↔ y.y mmHg". Neither one says that the result is the peak (maximum instantaneous) gradient, that a mean gradient can't be converted, or when the proximal velocity has to be included. Directly under the converter, the mitral and tricuspid tabs and the aortic Mean Gradient column grade by mean gradient. Two examples: a mitral peak velocity of 2 m/s converts to 16 mmHg, which the mitral tab's mean-gradient column calls severe (>10); an AS mean gradient of 40 mmHg typed in returns 3.16 m/s, a moderate velocity.
findings.fix: Label the field "Peak gradient" on both, and add one line: the mean gradient is traced from the Doppler envelope and can't be converted from a velocity. If the proximal (LVOT) velocity is over 1.5 m/s or Vmax is under 3.0 m/s, use ΔP = 4(Vmax² − Vproximal²) (ASE/EACVI 2017 p. 378).

findings.piece: Front-page quick calculator (shared/calculators/bernoulli.ts): formula, rounding, limits, citation
findings.says: Fields "Peak velocity" (m/s; min 0.1, max 10, step 0.01; placeholder 4.2) and "Pressure gradient" (mmHg; min 0, max 400, step 0.1; placeholder 70.6). compute fills the other field: a typed velocity above 0 gives 4v² to 0.1 mmHg, and a typed gradient of 0 or more gives √(ΔP/4) to 0.01 m/s. The headline reads "x.xx m/s ↔ y.y mmHg" with the detail "ΔP = 4v²"; otherwise it shows "Enter a peak velocity or a pressure gradient." implements: 'none'. Citation: "Baumgartner H et al. Recommendations on the echocardiographic assessment of aortic valve stenosis: a focused update from the EACVI and ASE. J Am Soc Echocardiogr 2017;30:372–392." Runs (docs/audit/batch-3/cases/bernoulli_module.results.md, 39 cases): every conversion equals the old page's run of the same input. A velocity of 0 or −4, a gradient of −1, and a run with no field just typed give the prompt. Blank and 'abc' are not read as numbers (the 4 'input not accepted' runs, as intended). When both fields hold values, the field just typed wins (4 m/s with 999 mmHg → 64.0). At the cut-offs the headline pairs a rounded velocity with the typed gradient: 63.9 mmHg → "4.00 m/s ↔ 63.9 mmHg", and 3.999 m/s → "4.00 m/s ↔ 64.0 mmHg".
